paragraphs.text: Μὴ κρίνετε, ἵνα μὴ κριθῆτε·
paragraphs.translit: Mē krinete, hina mē krithēte·

i18n.en: Do not judge, so that you may not be judged.

notes.official: *mē krinete hina mē krithēte* — 'do not judge, lest you be judged'. The judgment-section opens with a wisdom-tradition reciprocity-principle (cf. m.Sotah 1:7 'with whatever measure a person measures, it shall be measured to him'). The Matthean teaching critiques harsh-judgment-of-others within the community, not all-judgment-as-such. Davies-Allison ICC 1.668-672.

paragraphs.text: ἐν ᾧ γὰρ κρίματι κρίνετε κριθήσεσθε, καὶ ἐν ᾧ μέτρῳ μετρεῖτε μετρηθήσεται ὑμῖν.
paragraphs.translit: en hō gar krimati krinete krithēsesthe, kai en hō metrō metreite metrēthēsetai hymin.

i18n.en: For with the judgment you pronounce you will be judged, and with the measure you use it will be measured to you.

paragraphs.text: τί δὲ βλέπεις τὸ κάρφος τὸ ἐν τῷ ὀφθαλμῷ τοῦ ἀδελφοῦ σου, τὴν δὲ ἐν τῷ σῷ ὀφθαλμῷ δοκὸν οὐ κατανοεῖς;
paragraphs.translit: ti de blepeis to karphos to en tō ophthalmō tou adelphou sou, tēn de en tō sō ophthalmō dokon ou katanoeis?

i18n.en: Why do you see the speck that is in your brother's eye, but do not notice the beam that is in your own eye?

notes.official: *ti de blepeis to karphos to en tō ophthalmō tou adelphou sou* — the speck-and-plank hyperbole. Rabbinic-parallel: b.Arak. 16b 'remove the splinter from between your teeth, and they will say, remove the beam from between your eyes'. The hyperbolic rhetorical-style is characteristic of Jewish-wisdom and the Matthean Jesus-tradition.

paragraphs.text: ἢ πῶς ἐρεῖς τῷ ἀδελφῷ σου· Ἄφες ἐκβάλω τὸ κάρφος ἐκ τοῦ ὀφθαλμοῦ σου, καὶ ἰδοὺ ἡ δοκὸς ἐν τῷ ὀφθαλμῷ σοῦ;
paragraphs.translit: ē pōs ereis tō adelphō sou· Aphes ekbalō to karphos ek tou ophthalmou sou, kai idou hē dokos en tō ophthalmō sou?

i18n.en: Or how can you say to your brother, "Let me take the speck out of your eye," while behold, the beam is in your own eye?

paragraphs.text: ὑποκριτά, ἔκβαλε πρῶτον ἐκ τοῦ ὀφθαλμοῦ σοῦ τὴν δοκόν, καὶ τότε διαβλέψεις ἐκβαλεῖν τὸ κάρφος ἐκ τοῦ ὀφθαλμοῦ τοῦ ἀδελφοῦ σου.
paragraphs.translit: hypokrita, ekbale prōton ek tou ophthalmou sou tēn dokon, kai tote diablepseis ekbalein to karphos ek tou ophthalmou tou adelphou sou.

i18n.en: You hypocrite, first take the beam out of your own eye, and then you will see clearly to take the speck out of your brother's eye.

paragraphs.text: Μὴ δῶτε τὸ ἅγιον τοῖς κυσίν, μηδὲ βάλητε τοὺς μαργαρίτας ὑμῶν ἔμπροσθεν τῶν χοίρων, μήποτε καταπατήσουσιν αὐτοὺς ἐν τοῖς ποσὶν αὐτῶν καὶ στραφέντες ῥήξωσιν ὑμᾶς.
paragraphs.translit: Mē dōte to hagion tois kysin, mēde balēte tous margaritas hymōn emprosthen tōn choirōn, mēpote katapatēsousin autous en tois posin autōn kai straphentes rhēxōsin hymas.

i18n.en: Do not give what is holy to dogs, nor cast your pearls before swine, lest they trample them under their feet, and turn and tear you to pieces.

notes.official: *mē dōte to hagion tois kysin mēde balēte tous margaritas hymōn emprosthen tōn choirōn* — 'do not give what is holy to the dogs ... pearls before swine'. Aphoristic-wisdom protecting sacred-teaching from desecration. The verse has been deployed in early-Christian Eucharistic discipline (Didache 9:5); the original Matthean horizon is broader-than-Eucharistic. Davies-Allison ICC 1.674-678.

paragraphs.text: Αἰτεῖτε, καὶ δοθήσεται ὑμῖν· ζητεῖτε, καὶ εὑρήσετε· κρούετε, καὶ ἀνοιγήσεται ὑμῖν.
paragraphs.translit: Aiteite, kai dothēsetai hymin· zēteite, kai heurēsete· krouete, kai anoigēsetai hymin.

i18n.en: Ask, and it will be given to you; seek, and you will find; knock, and it will be opened to you.

notes.official: *aiteite ... zēteite ... krouete* — the three-fold ask-seek-knock aphorism. Generally treated as a Q-source saying preserved in both Matthew and Lk 11:9-13. The Matthean *patēr hymōn ho en ouranois* (v.11) closes the section with the Matthean-distinctive Father-in-the-heavens-formula echoing the Lord's Prayer (6:9).

paragraphs.text: πᾶς γὰρ ὁ αἰτῶν λαμβάνει καὶ ὁ ζητῶν εὑρίσκει καὶ τῷ κρούοντι ἀνοιγήσεται.
paragraphs.translit: pas gar ho aitōn lambanei kai ho zētōn heuriskei kai tō krouonti anoigēsetai.

i18n.en: For everyone who asks receives, and the one who seeks finds, and to the one who knocks it will be opened.

paragraphs.text: ἢ τίς ἐστιν ἐξ ὑμῶν ἄνθρωπος, ὃν αἰτήσει ὁ υἱὸς αὐτοῦ ἄρτον — μὴ λίθον ἐπιδώσει αὐτῷ;
paragraphs.translit: ē tis estin ex hymōn anthrōpos, hon aitēsei ho huios autou arton — mē lithon epidōsei autō?

i18n.en: Or what man is there among you, whose son will ask him for bread — will he give him a stone?

paragraphs.text: ἢ καὶ ἰχθὺν αἰτήσει — μὴ ὄφιν ἐπιδώσει αὐτῷ;
paragraphs.translit: ē kai ichthyn aitēsei — mē ophin epidōsei autō?

i18n.en: Or if he asks for a fish, will he give him a snake?

paragraphs.text: εἰ οὖν ὑμεῖς πονηροὶ ὄντες οἴδατε δόματα ἀγαθὰ διδόναι τοῖς τέκνοις ὑμῶν, πόσῳ μᾶλλον ὁ πατὴρ ὑμῶν ὁ ἐν τοῖς οὐρανοῖς δώσει ἀγαθὰ τοῖς αἰτοῦσιν αὐτόν.
paragraphs.translit: ei oun hymeis ponēroi ontes oidate domata agatha didonai tois teknois hymōn, posō mallon ho patēr hymōn ho en tois ouranois dōsei agatha tois aitousin auton.

i18n.en: If you then, being evil, know how to give good gifts to your children, how much more will your Father who is in the heavens give good things to those who ask him.

paragraphs.text: Πάντα οὖν ὅσα ἐὰν θέλητε ἵνα ποιῶσιν ὑμῖν οἱ ἄνθρωποι, οὕτως καὶ ὑμεῖς ποιεῖτε αὐτοῖς· οὗτος γάρ ἐστιν ὁ νόμος καὶ οἱ προφῆται.
paragraphs.translit: Panta oun hosa ean thelēte hina poiōsin hymin hoi anthrōpoi, houtōs kai hymeis poieite autois· houtos gar estin ho nomos kai hoi prophētai.

i18n.en: Therefore everything that you wish people to do for you, so also do you to them; for this is the Law and the Prophets.

notes.official: **The Golden Rule.** *Panta oun hosa ean thelēte hina poiōsin hymin hoi anthrōpoi, houtōs kai hymeis poieite autois* — positive-formulation. Cross-corpus parallel to Hillel's b.Shabbat 31a negative-formulation 'what is hateful to you, do not do to your fellow' (the Hillel-rule explicitly identified as 'the whole Torah'); Tobit 4:15 (negative-formulation, 3rd-2nd c. BCE); Confucius Analects 15.23 (negative-formulation, 6th-5th c. BCE); Letter of Aristeas 207. The Matthean closing *houtos gar estin ho nomos kai hoi prophētai* explicitly identifies the rule as a Torah-summary, structurally paralleling Mt 22:40 and forming inclusio with Mt 5:17. See `golden-rule-mt-7-12-hillel-cross-corpus`.

paragraphs.text: Εἰσέλθατε διὰ τῆς στενῆς πύλης· ὅτι πλατεῖα ἡ πύλη καὶ εὐρύχωρος ἡ ὁδὸς ἡ ἀπάγουσα εἰς τὴν ἀπώλειαν, καὶ πολλοί εἰσιν οἱ εἰσερχόμενοι δι' αὐτῆς·
paragraphs.translit: Eiselthate dia tēs stenēs pylēs· hoti plateia hē pylē kai eurychōros hē hodos hē apagousa eis tēn apōleian, kai polloi eisin hoi eiserchomenoi di' autēs·

i18n.en: Enter through the narrow gate; for wide is the gate and broad the way that leads to destruction, and many are those who enter through it.

notes.official: *eiselthate dia tēs stenēs pylēs* — 'enter through the narrow gate'. The two-ways tradition is rooted in Jewish-wisdom (Deut 30:15-20 the life-and-death paths; Ps 1 the two-ways psalm; Jer 21:8 'I set before you the way of life and the way of death'; Sir 21:10; Did. 1:1 'two ways, one of life and one of death'). Davies-Allison ICC 1.694-698.

paragraphs.text: τί στενὴ ἡ πύλη καὶ τεθλιμμένη ἡ ὁδὸς ἡ ἀπάγουσα εἰς τὴν ζωήν, καὶ ὀλίγοι εἰσὶν οἱ εὑρίσκοντες αὐτήν.
paragraphs.translit: ti stenē hē pylē kai tethlimmenē hē hodos hē apagousa eis tēn zōēn, kai oligoi eisin hoi heuriskontes autēn.

i18n.en: How narrow is the gate and constricted the way that leads to life, and few are those who find it!

paragraphs.text: Προσέχετε ἀπὸ τῶν ψευδοπροφητῶν, οἵτινες ἔρχονται πρὸς ὑμᾶς ἐν ἐνδύμασι προβάτων, ἔσωθεν δέ εἰσιν λύκοι ἅρπαγες.
paragraphs.translit: Prosechete apo tōn pseudoprophētōn, hoitines erchontai pros hymas en endymasi probatōn, esōthen de eisin lykoi harpages.

i18n.en: Beware of the false prophets, who come to you in sheep's clothing, but inwardly are ravenous wolves.

notes.official: *prosechete apo tōn pseudoprophētōn* — 'beware of false prophets'. The false-prophets warning continues the eschatological-test-of-discernment tradition (Deut 13:2-6; Jer 23:9-40; Ezek 13). The Matthean horizon addresses both external-false-prophets and intra-community false-teachers (Mt 24:11, 24).

paragraphs.text: ἀπὸ τῶν καρπῶν αὐτῶν ἐπιγνώσεσθε αὐτούς· μήτι συλλέγουσιν ἀπὸ ἀκανθῶν σταφυλὰς ἢ ἀπὸ τριβόλων σῦκα;
paragraphs.translit: apo tōn karpōn autōn epignōsesthe autous· mēti syllegousin apo akanthōn staphylas ē apo tribolōn syka?

i18n.en: By their fruits you will recognize them. Do they gather grapes from thornbushes, or figs from thistles?

paragraphs.text: οὕτως πᾶν δένδρον ἀγαθὸν καρποὺς καλοὺς ποιεῖ, τὸ δὲ σαπρὸν δένδρον καρποὺς πονηροὺς ποιεῖ·
paragraphs.translit: houtōs pan dendron agathon karpous kalous poiei, to de sapron dendron karpous ponērous poiei·

i18n.en: So every good tree bears good fruit, but the rotten tree bears bad fruit.

paragraphs.text: οὐ δύναται δένδρον ἀγαθὸν καρποὺς πονηροὺς ποιεῖν, οὐδὲ δένδρον σαπρὸν καρποὺς καλοὺς ποιεῖν.
paragraphs.translit: ou dynatai dendron agathon karpous ponērous poiein, oude dendron sapron karpous kalous poiein.

i18n.en: A good tree cannot bear bad fruit, nor can a rotten tree bear good fruit.

paragraphs.text: πᾶν δένδρον μὴ ποιοῦν καρπὸν καλὸν ἐκκόπτεται καὶ εἰς πῦρ βάλλεται.
paragraphs.translit: pan dendron mē poioun karpon kalon ekkoptetai kai eis pyr balletai.

i18n.en: Every tree that does not bear good fruit is cut down and thrown into the fire.

paragraphs.text: ἄρα γε ἀπὸ τῶν καρπῶν αὐτῶν ἐπιγνώσεσθε αὐτούς.
paragraphs.translit: ara ge apo tōn karpōn autōn epignōsesthe autous.

i18n.en: So then, by their fruits you will recognize them.

paragraphs.text: Οὐ πᾶς ὁ λέγων μοι· Κύριε κύριε, εἰσελεύσεται εἰς τὴν βασιλείαν τῶν οὐρανῶν, ἀλλ' ὁ ποιῶν τὸ θέλημα τοῦ πατρός μου τοῦ ἐν τοῖς οὐρανοῖς.
paragraphs.translit: Ou pas ho legōn moi· Kyrie kyrie, eiseleusetai eis tēn basileian tōn ouranōn, all' ho poiōn to thelēma tou patros mou tou en tois ouranois.

i18n.en: Not everyone who says to me, "Lord, Lord," will enter the kingdom of the heavens, but the one who does the will of my Father who is in the heavens.

notes.official: *ou pas ho legōn moi 'kyrie, kyrie' eiseleusetai eis tēn basileian tōn ouranōn, all' ho poiōn to thelēma tou patros mou tou en tois ouranois* — 'not everyone who says to me Lord, Lord ... but the one who does the will of my Father in the heavens'. The Matthean-distinctive doing-the-will closing of the SM-ethic. The kingdom-of-the-heavens phrase per the Matthean redactional-pattern. See `kingdom-of-heaven-basileia-tōn-ouranōn-mt-distinctive-cross-corpus-hebrew-malkhut-shamayim`.

paragraphs.text: πολλοὶ ἐροῦσίν μοι ἐν ἐκείνῃ τῇ ἡμέρᾳ· Κύριε κύριε, οὐ τῷ σῷ ὀνόματι ἐπροφητεύσαμεν, καὶ τῷ σῷ ὀνόματι δαιμόνια ἐξεβάλομεν, καὶ τῷ σῷ ὀνόματι δυνάμεις πολλὰς ἐποιήσαμεν;
paragraphs.translit: polloi erousin moi en ekeinē tē hēmera· Kyrie kyrie, ou tō sō onomati eprophēteusamen, kai tō sō onomati daimonia exebalomen, kai tō sō onomati dynameis pollas epoiēsamen?

i18n.en: Many will say to me on that day, "Lord, Lord, did we not prophesy in your name, and in your name cast out demons, and in your name perform many mighty works?"

paragraphs.text: καὶ τότε ὁμολογήσω αὐτοῖς ὅτι Οὐδέποτε ἔγνων ὑμᾶς· ἀποχωρεῖτε ἀπ' ἐμοῦ οἱ ἐργαζόμενοι τὴν ἀνομίαν.
paragraphs.translit: kai tote homologēsō autois hoti Oudepote egnōn hymas· apochōreite ap' emou hoi ergazomenoi tēn anomian.

i18n.en: And then I will declare to them, "I never knew you; depart from me, you workers of lawlessness."

paragraphs.text: Πᾶς οὖν ὅστις ἀκούει μου τοὺς λόγους τούτους καὶ ποιεῖ αὐτούς, ὁμοιωθήσεται ἀνδρὶ φρονίμῳ, ὅστις ᾠκοδόμησεν αὐτοῦ τὴν οἰκίαν ἐπὶ τὴν πέτραν.
paragraphs.translit: Pas oun hostis akouei mou tous logous toutous kai poiei autous, homoiōthēsetai andri phronimō, hostis ōkodomēsen autou tēn oikian epi tēn petran.

i18n.en: Therefore everyone who hears these words of mine and does them will be likened to a wise man who built his house upon the rock.

notes.official: **The two builders parable.** *pas oun hostis akouei mou tous logous toutous kai poiei autous* — the SM's closing-parable contrasting hearer-and-doer with hearer-only. The petra (rock) vs ammos (sand) foundations + the storm-of-judgment imagery; the rock-foundation parallel echoes Isa 28:16 (the cornerstone-in-Zion).

paragraphs.text: καὶ κατέβη ἡ βροχὴ καὶ ἦλθον οἱ ποταμοὶ καὶ ἔπνευσαν οἱ ἄνεμοι καὶ προσέπεσαν τῇ οἰκίᾳ ἐκείνῃ, καὶ οὐκ ἔπεσεν, τεθεμελίωτο γὰρ ἐπὶ τὴν πέτραν.
paragraphs.translit: kai katebē hē brochē kai ēlthon hoi potamoi kai epneusan hoi anemoi kai prosepesan tē oikia ekeinē, kai ouk epesen, tethemeliōto gar epi tēn petran.

i18n.en: And the rain came down, and the rivers came, and the winds blew, and beat upon that house; and it did not fall, for it had been founded upon the rock.

paragraphs.text: καὶ πᾶς ὁ ἀκούων μου τοὺς λόγους τούτους καὶ μὴ ποιῶν αὐτοὺς ὁμοιωθήσεται ἀνδρὶ μωρῷ, ὅστις ᾠκοδόμησεν αὐτοῦ τὴν οἰκίαν ἐπὶ τὴν ἄμμον.
paragraphs.translit: kai pas ho akouōn mou tous logous toutous kai mē poiōn autous homoiōthēsetai andri mōrō, hostis ōkodomēsen autou tēn oikian epi tēn ammon.

i18n.en: And everyone who hears these words of mine and does not do them will be likened to a foolish man who built his house upon the sand.

paragraphs.text: καὶ κατέβη ἡ βροχὴ καὶ ἦλθον οἱ ποταμοὶ καὶ ἔπνευσαν οἱ ἄνεμοι καὶ προσέκοψαν τῇ οἰκίᾳ ἐκείνῃ, καὶ ἔπεσεν, καὶ ἦν ἡ πτῶσις αὐτῆς μεγάλη.
paragraphs.translit: kai katebē hē brochē kai ēlthon hoi potamoi kai epneusan hoi anemoi kai prosekopsan tē oikia ekeinē, kai epesen, kai ēn hē ptōsis autēs megalē.

i18n.en: And the rain came down, and the rivers came, and the winds blew, and struck against that house; and it fell — and great was its fall.

paragraphs.text: Καὶ ἐγένετο ὅτε ἐτέλεσεν ὁ Ἰησοῦς τοὺς λόγους τούτους, ἐξεπλήσσοντο οἱ ὄχλοι ἐπὶ τῇ διδαχῇ αὐτοῦ·
paragraphs.translit: Kai egeneto hote etelesen ho Iēsous tous logous toutous, exeplēssonto hoi ochloi epi tē didachē autou·

i18n.en: And it came to pass, when Jesus had finished these words, the crowds were astonished at his teaching;

notes.official: *kai egeneto hote etelesen ho Iēsous tous logous toutous* — 'and when Jesus finished these sayings'. The Matthean transition-formula closing the first of the five Matthean discourse-blocks (the SM is the first; the structure is generally treated as a Matthean Pentateuchal-typology with five discourse-blocks paralleling the five books of Moses). Davies-Allison ICC 1.725-727.

paragraphs.text: ἦν γὰρ διδάσκων αὐτοὺς ὡς ἐξουσίαν ἔχων καὶ οὐχ ὡς οἱ γραμματεῖς αὐτῶν.
paragraphs.translit: ēn gar didaskōn autous hōs exousian echōn kai ouch hōs hoi grammateis autōn.

i18n.en: for he was teaching them as one having authority, and not as their scribes.

notes.official: *ēn gar didaskōn autous hōs exousian echōn, kai ouch hōs hoi grammateis* — 'for he taught them as one having authority, and not as their scribes'. The Matthean Jesus' teaching-authority claim parallels the Mt 28:18 final authority-grant (*edothē moi pasa exousia*) — both deploy *exousia*. The polemical-comparison with the scribes is intra-Jewish, not anti-Jewish.
